caption: Figure 6: Overview of Optuna 's system design. Each worker executes one instance of an objective function in each study . The Objective function runs its trial using Optuna APIs. When the API is invoked, the objective function accesses the shared storage and obtains the information of the past studies from the storage when necessary. Each worker runs the objective function independently and shares the progress of the current study via the storage.
description:

caption: Figure 11: The transition of average test errors of simplified AlexNet for SVHN dataset. Figure (a) illustrates the e ect of pruning mechanisms on TPE and random search. Figure (b) illustrates the e ect of the number of workers on the performance. Figure (c) plots the test errors against the number of trials for di erent number of workers. Note that the number of workers has no e ect on the relation between the number of executed trials and the test error. The result also shows the superiority of ASHA pruning over median pruning.
description:
This figure consists of three line graphs, labeled (a), (b), and (c), showing the average test error of a simplified AlexNet model for the SVHN dataset. Graph (a) compares different pruning mechanisms (Random, TPE, Median Pruning, Successive Halving Pruning) over elapsed time. Graph (b) shows the effect of the number of workers on performance. Graph (c) plots test errors against the number of trials for different worker sizes. The highest average test error is observed in the Random series in graph (a), while the lowest is in the TPE + Successive Halving Pruning series. In graph (b), the series with size=1 has the highest error, and size=8 has the lowest. Graph (c) shows that the number of workers does not affect the relation between trials and test error.

Text in figure: "Elapsed time (min)", "Number of trials", "Average test error", "Random", "TPE", "Random + Median Pruning", "TPE + Median Pruning", "Random + Successive Halving Pruning", "TPE + Successive Halving Pruning", "size=1", "size=2", "size=4", "size=8".
